$comment: The per-kit equivalents of the modernity lint (UI-KITS.md §7.3), as source rules over each native kit. Read by bin/kit-lint.mjs (zero dependencies, so every kit's CI lane can run it with plain Node) and by `pnpm ui:lint`. A file whose first 400 bytes say GENERATED is skipped (the brand generator owns it). A line containing `ui-lint: allow <rule-id>` and a reason is exempt from that rule. Debt that existed when this landed is in kit-debt.json; the lint fails on anything new and on debt that is gone.

rules.says: No .buttonBorderShape(.roundedRectangle) override: iOS 26 buttons keep the system capsule shape.
RTL-safe layout: .leading/.trailing, never .left/.right.
No default system alerts for anything the kit owns; use the kit's sheet or inline confirm (a destructive Replace may use .confirmationDialog, SIGN-IN.md D-80).
No all-caps labels.
No colour literal outside the generated tokens (KitTokens, BrandTokens).
Android uses the M3 filled field, never the outlined or notched one.
No Icons.Filled from the legacy set; use the Material Symbols subset the kit ships.
RTL-safe layout: Start/End, never Left/Right or the absolute variants.
No stock indeterminate spinner: the M3 Expressive LoadingIndicator inline, the countdown ring or a skeleton.
No AlertDialog with stock buttons for anything the kit owns.
No engine AcceptDialog / ConfirmationDialog / OS.alert for anything the kit owns.
No CheckBox where a switch is meant: the kit's one switch (CheckButton themed by the brand).
RTL-safe layout: let layout_direction mirror the controls; no hard-coded left or right alignment.
No all-caps labels.
No colour literal outside the generated tokens and the brand theme.
No default system dialogs for anything the kit owns.
No check box where a switch is meant: the kit's one switch.
RTL-safe layout: Qt mirrors AlignLeft/AlignRight in RTL, but not QSS physical margins or AlignAbsolute.
No colour literal outside the generated theme (Theme.qml, the .qss files).
RTL-safe layout: pad with cell-aware spans and let the terminal's bidi lay the line out; no left or right justification.
No hand-written SGR: every role's parameters come from the generated ANSI tables (polaris_key/ui/ansi.py); only the writer in text.py emits them.
No colour literal outside the generated tokens and the accent resolver.
No stock spinner: the braille spinner in mute from the generated tables, at 80 ms a frame.
